tldr: Public comment submissions from Oregon Prosperity Council survey respondents (individuals and organizations) on economic priorities. Dominant themes: aging workforce strategy and skills training, tax code reform (SB 1507, QBI deduction), K-12 education underfunding since Measure 5, housing and urban land-use shortage, permitting delays, childcare as workforce enabler, climate policy trade-offs, and regulatory burden. Respondents show divided views on climate regulation costs versus business opportunity.

bullets.text: Aging workforce critical: one in four Oregon jobs held by workers 55+; more residents 65+ than youth under 18; HECC struggling to meet educational attainment goals for adults 40+
SB 1507 repeal requested to restore SBQS tax benefit for startups; removal of benefit threatens investment and could drive founders, shareholders, investors out of state
K-12 chronically underfunded since Measure 5 (1990s); schools facing escalating liability and insurance costs; revenue reform via QEM model and accountability proposed
Climate Protection Program criticized for raising energy costs without guaranteed emissions reductions or business investment incentives; immediate pause recommended
Permitting delays and SDC fees identified as major barriers; developers face high time/cost hurdles; system described as baked to delay or block development
Urban land supply shortage: 42,200 net acres needed by 2045 to accommodate 491,347 housing units; 81% required in cities of 10,000+ population
Childcare and early education positioned as workforce enabler; employee retention and family recruitment tied to childcare access and affordability
UBI programs expanding nationally: 18 states with UBI in 2025, 57 programs total, 12 in California; proof-of-concept success documented
Clean energy incentives needed (EV rebates, solar, heat pump support) to attract businesses and workers; grid capacity and permitting challenges impeding adoption
Preschool for All program cited as national model; universal free pre-K gaining momentum as competitive workforce retention and family support tool
